title: An Analysis of the Relationship between Words within the Voynich Manuscript
authors: Andrew Caruana, Colin Layfield, John Abela
summary: The authors compare directional word-pair frequencies in a Voynich transliteration and English and Italian texts with shuffled versions. Their exploratory comparison reports an excess of directionally skewed pairs in the manuscript, smaller than the excess in the comparison texts; it does not test a meaningless-text generator or establish that the text is linguistic.
established: The analysis uses ZL version 1r and selected Bible books, two Shakespeare plays and Dante's Divina Commedia. It removes frequent words using empirically selected percentages and counts pairs within a three-word window; a pair is skewed if its count exceeds its reverse by more than five (sections 2.1–2.3).

Figure 2 compares each original with the average of three random shuffles. The authors report that the Voynich original has slightly more than twice the skewed-pair ratio of its shuffled counterpart, with a smaller original-to-shuffle gap than in the comparison texts (section 3.1).

For 10,000-word randomly selected segments, averaged over three runs, the paper reports an approximately inverse relationship between unique-word ratio and skewed-pair ratio across the works (section 3.2).

open.question: How do the skewed-pair and unique-word measures behave on texts transformed by historically plausible ciphers, as compared with their unencoded sources?
open.check: Apply the published measures and prespecified frequency filtering to matched plaintext and cipher variants, using multiple samples and fixed random seeds; compare the resulting changes with the manuscript's public and hidden pages.
